content.body:
Almost doomed by the bureaucracy of the RLM prior to its maiden flight, the Messerschmitt Bf 109 went on to become the most mass-produced German fighter of the war. Its design was simple: a compact slender airframe with plenty of power and an amazing climb rate. The 109's combat lineage started in the Spanish Civil war in the mid-thirties.
By the outbreak of WWII, the E model was already a tried and true, combat-tested fighter aircraft, and by the war's end, just five years later, the highest scoring aerial aces in the history of air combat had all exclusively flown Bf 109's.
The E-1 model is fast and although lightly armed it is easily the best turner of the 109's, this plane is as at home in a turn fight as it is in a fast, diving attack. With coordinated wingman tactics the Emil can be effective against any enemy type, but alone its speed and climb rate must be relied on to survive an encounter with bad odds. Combine its overall good performance with a cool-headed and confident pilot and the E-1 can do better than some might think. Against the RAF you must resist the temptation to turn flight exclusively, as both the Spitfire and Hurricane can slightly out-turn with the Bf 109E-1, if pressed to the point of a pure turning duel over several turns around the circle.
However, climbing turns are a different story completely and can neutralize an enemy's turning advantage quickly in the 109's favor.
The E is sometimes referred to as the "Emil" for the "E" model designation.
